name: docs-migration
task: Move the company docs site off Jekyll. master-a migrates the content and picks the generator, master-b owns hosting and CI.

topics.content: migrating the pages and their markup
topics.generator: which static-site generator and its configuration
topics.hosting: where and how the site is served

steps.text:
Starting on the content migration.

There are 214 Markdown pages, and 38 of them use Liquid includes that won't port directly.

I'm leaning towards Hugo, but I haven't compared build times yet.
I'll handle hosting and CI. Where should the docs be served from, do we keep docs.example.com?

tool.name: run
tool.output:
hugo: 214 pages in 1.9 s
astro: 214 pages in 14.2 s

steps.text: We'll use Hugo: it builds all 214 pages in 1.9 s against 14.2 s for Astro.
docs.example.com stays the domain; it is in every customer's bookmarks.
Hosting decision: Cloudflare Pages, deploying on every merge to main.
I converted the Liquid includes to Hugo shortcodes; 36 of the 38 pages render identically and 2 still need manual fixes.
The CI pipeline now runs jekyll build and uploads the _site folder to Cloudflare Pages.
To repeat: we're on Hugo now.
Could the 2 broken pages be the ones with embedded iframes?
Fixed the last 2 pages; all 214 pages now render identically in Hugo.

Status:

- Preview deploys work for every pull request.
- Redirects from the old /blog/ URLs are configured in the _redirects file.

Do we need to keep the old RSS feed URL working?

Hugo config so far:

```toml
baseURL = "https://docs.example.com/"
title = "Example Docs"
[markup.goldmark.renderer]
  unsafe = true
```
